rows.claim: The bibliography's three-wave self-audit found the same failure mode each wave: real, checkable sources cited one step stronger than what they showed (Helium's 1.56x stretched into an unsourced >35% claim at line 1108; Leyline's +14.3 pp transposed into 241pp at lines 1270 and 1276), so every citation must be assigned the verb its source actually licenses; citation-supported is not claim-supported.
rows.quote: every citation gets the verb the source actually licenses (*shows*, *reports*, *proposes*, *does not test*) instead of the verb the surrounding prose wants (*mandates*, *demonstrates*, *proves*).
rows.steal: Before banking any mined claim into a steal card or rib, write the verb check in one sitting: name which verb the primary licenses (shows, reports, proposes, does not test) and downgrade the claim to that verb; landing spot is the next digest or steal card under corpus/steal/.
rows.falsifier: A self-mined bibliography wave whose stretched-citation error rate is zero across all entries, while verb-matched entries still need correction, would invert this law.

rows.claim: An architecture's two load-bearing claims each had their canonical citation in a different field from the bibliography the builders drew from (Dynamo/Merkle for the append-only record, Hurlbert for replication measurement), nine frontier models plus the fleet missed them in the same direction, and mining adjacent fields must therefore be deliberate; cross-confirmed this ask: the estate's 2026-10-01 LIBRARIAN commit 962e41054 landed founding-law texts Dynamo 2007 and Lamport 1998, two of exactly the debts this document names at lines 63 and 104.
rows.quote: an architecture that intends to be sovereign should mine adjacent fields on purpose, not by accident of whoever happens to be in the room.
rows.steal: In one sitting, grep corpus/steal and memory/rib for Hurlbert and pseudoreplication; if absent, attach the Hurlbert 1984 citation to the next measurement-doctrine or Red-Ledger row so the replication half of the named debt lands like the Dynamo half already did.
rows.falsifier: A seat population whose canon is uniform enough that blind spots stay uncorrelated across models and fields would remove the thesis's payoff.

rows.quote: For Mag, the valuable artifact is not merely a copy of the 321GB-class weight file. It is a model passport containing:
rows.steal: In one sitting, create configs/model_passports/glm-5.3-flash.json holding the 12-field schema with vendor claims labeled vendor-reported and unknowns copied from the source's own list (lines 194-208), then file a TICKET_LEDGER row pointing at it.

rows.claim: The failure shape is double: run the tool on the wrong surface first, then over-rotate to declaring the environment incapable, when the real surface was one docker hop away (mag-sovereign:8001) and documented in a file the seat already owned (api_gateway.py); the fix that stuck was a one-liner helper (mag_api.mjs) plus a TOOLS.md row so no seat rediscovers it, not a one-time correction.
rows.quote: The truth was sitting one docker hop away on 172.19.0.5, and api_gateway.py documents the whole surface.
rows.steal: When a surface check fails, spend one sitting probing the second-degree surface (network neighbor, sibling port, parent config, the routing table the seat owns) before writing any cannot-do claim, and land the finding as a tool-table row, not just a chat correction.
rows.falsifier: A declared-owner tool table that provably enumerates every reachable surface, where a failed check correctly meant no capability existed, would remove the law's payoff.

rows.quote: Most-Variable Components First: Place elements that change most frequently between generations (like specific rules or themes) at the beginning of prompts, while stable elements (like basic game mechanics) should come later
rows.steal: In one sitting, reorder one estate game-build prompt (the trails or FLOW_LEDGER game surface) stable-core-first with variable parameters last and check one serving log for a cache-hit improvement before adopting the ordering broadly.
